title: TextMorph
tagline: System-wide, privacy-first multimodal AI writing assistant & floating toolbar for Android powered by multi-engine local LLM inference
hero_description: A system-wide, privacy-first multimodal AI writing assistant & floating toolbar for Android. Powered by a modular multi-engine architecture supporting Google LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp, and OpenAI-compatible APIs to run any open foundation model locally with zero-copy memory mapping, slash commands, and an embedded server.

engines.title: Supported Local & API Inference Engines
engines.litert: Google LiteRT-LM (Mobile GPU/NPU acceleration, zero-copy mmap)
engines.llamacpp: llama.cpp Runtime (Universal GGUF quantized models on CPU/GPU)
engines.openai: OpenAI-Compatible APIs (Embedded Ktor server on 127.0.0.1:8080 and external endpoints)

features.multi_engine: Multi-Engine On-Device AI: Run models via LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp, or connect via OpenAI-compatible endpoints directly on mobile silicon with zero cloud latency and total privacy.
features.floating_bar: System-Wide Floating AI Pill: Non-intrusive AccessibilityService overlay that anchors above active input fields without stealing keyboard focus (FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE).
features.zero_copy: Universal Zero-Copy Downloads Loader: Memory-maps multi-gigabyte models directly via Linux mmap and ParcelFileDescriptor without duplicate flash storage overhead.
features.slash_commands: Universal Slash Commands: Trigger AI transformations in any text box by typing /fix, /summarize, /fr (French), or /ar (Arabic) with instant in-place buffer replacement.
features.server: Embedded Localhost OpenAI Server: Lightweight Ktor CIO HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8080 exposing standard OpenAI-compatible streaming chat completions for Termux and local tools.
features.vision: Multimodal Vision Screen Assist: MediaProjection integration captures active screen context and provides instant on-device multimodal reasoning without cloud exposure.

architecture.layer_runtime_desc: Hardware-accelerated edge inference executing any open-weights LLM locally. Modular engine abstraction supports Google LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp, and local/remote OpenAI-compatible backends.
